correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and initial northward drainage
correspondence.finding: Detailed imagery shows small ponds and narrow dark drainage traces in the initial rocky terrain. The selected northward corridor is located, but a continuous connection from the chosen opening through every initial pond is not securely established.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper pond sequence and northward bend
correspondence.finding: The upper detail shows a cluster of elongated waterbodies near the selected bend. Cloud partly obscures the continuation, and multiple narrow surface traces prevent treating proximity to those ponds as proof of the complete selected passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward transition from rocky terrain to wetland
correspondence.finding: The overview locates a northwest-trending drainage setting across the rocky margin into the lowland. It does not distinguish all selected small channels and joins along this transition.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower pond-rich wetland corridor
correspondence.finding: Numerous rounded ponds and several shallow drainage corridors are visible in the lower plain. The image establishes the wetland setting, while the selected sequence of pond passages and its connection to the final coastal branch remain ambiguous.

correspondence.component_scope: Final coastal approach and actual receiving shore
correspondence.finding: The terminal detail shows a small drainage meeting a broad coastal flat, with several neighboring inland channels. The selected receiving shore is on Foxe Basin, south of the separate large northern river mouth. The specific connection from the chosen lower branch into the observed small outlet remains unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen Cancire opening, Quebrada Honda and Palagua upper corridor, missing eastern connection, and Goascorán receiving interval
correspondence.finding: The actual northern opening is on the Cancire-labeled valley near Guajiquiro, not an assumed source of the lower Goascorán name. The selected upper line continues south along the Quebrada Honda-labeled valley into the Mercedes sheet and meets Río Palagua, then follows Palagua east to that sheet edge. The end of this fragment reappears on the independently inspected Aramecina sheet in the Goascorán receiving corridor. The intervening eastern upper/middle turn is not established by an allowed original.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped middle Goascorán interval and unresolved late southwestern continuation
correspondence.finding: The first six stored path parts and the beginning of the next correspond at corridor scale to the repeatedly labelled Río Goascorán: below the Caridad/Pescado confluence setting, past Concepción de Oriente and around the bends west of Aramecina. The selected line remains on Goascorán rather than taking the eastern Apasapo approach. The later southwestward continuation leaves the western coverage of the inspected Aramecina map.

correspondence.component_scope: Separate short mainstem fragment and both joining connections
correspondence.finding: This short separate selected mainstem fragment is retained as its own component. Neither its beginning and ending joins nor its intervening channel was observed in an allowed primary map; a nearby/receiving Goascorán label is not extended over it by inference.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river bends and delta approach
correspondence.finding: The selected lower southward and eastward-turning corridor, followed by its delta approach, was not established by allowed originals. The originally selected Langue and Bahía Chismuyo sheets both carry restrictive distribution notices, so their geography is excluded.

correspondence.component_scope: Western terminal passage and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The actual terminal-bearing fragment turns northwest and then west before its final southwestward ending. This distinctive selected terminal cannot be replaced by a generic Goascorán-to-Gulf statement. Both relevant coastal-sheet originals were excluded for printed restricted distribution; the independent ICJ1992 judgment original was unavailable after HTTP403, and no discovery excerpt is used as evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen_headward_opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening lies among small upland waterbodies and pale snow/ice-bearing channels. Readable imagery shows these features and the larger lake to the southwest, but local cloud and ambiguous branching prevent establishing the selected continuous opening-to-lake connection. Nearby waterbodies are not used as proof of that through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: upper_lake_passage
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor corresponds at ordinary scale to the western side of the upper large lake and its southwestern lake margin. The lake itself is geographically readable; no lake name is assigned. Its selected incoming connection is separately pending.

correspondence.component_scope: southern_transfer_and_turn
correspondence.finding: The upper lake has a readable westward outlet-valley setting, but the acquired southern-half detail does not establish the selected extended southwest-to-west-to-north U-shaped transfer. Parts of the terrain are cloudy and show branching shallow channels. A nearby visible westward valley is not substituted for the chosen southern route.

correspondence.component_scope: western_rejoining_valley
correspondence.finding: Farther northwest, a chain of small elongated waterbodies and a visible valley channel correspond to the selected approach to the westernmost turn, followed by the northeast continuation. Patchy snow/ice is visible in this corridor; no glacier-crossing or current-flow claim is made. The upstream connection from the southern loop remains separately pending.

correspondence.component_scope: middle_northeast_corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected northeast corridor follows a visible river through a confined-to-braided valley. Side-stream joins are visible, including a larger eastern-side join before the broad alluvial approach to the next lake. The local source correspondence does not resolve the distant opening.

correspondence.component_scope: large_through_lake
correspondence.finding: The river reaches the southern embayment of a large irregular lake across an alluvial plain. The selected northward passage traverses its western basin and long narrow northern arm. The continuous waterbody is readable; no lake name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: northern_lake_outlet_and_join
correspondence.finding: A visible outlet continues north from the long narrow lake arm into the lower eastward river corridor. The junction with the separate valley arriving from the northwest is visible at ordinary scale.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_eastward_corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor turns east at the northern junction and continues along the visibly connected broad lower river valley toward Koluktoo Bay. The separate incoming northwest valley is not treated as the selected path.

correspondence.component_scope: actual_marine_terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower river reaches the extensive alluvial/delta margin in the northwestern corner of Koluktoo Bay. ARC402 chapter4 paragraph176 independently names the river entering this corner as Robertson River. Together the prose and imagery support the actual sea terminal and downstream identity at ordinary regional scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western small-water opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in the small-lake and stream country at the southern edge of the Washburn Lake sheet. The original accounts for its southward small-water approach into the Cambridge Bay sheet. No independent name for this initial feeder or ultimate natural source is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper lake succession and northward return
correspondence.finding: The original adjoining sheets show the selected upper small waters, larger elongated waters and eastward/northward approach into the upper Ekalluk corridor. The sheet boundary is a cartographic boundary, not a river barrier. Individual feeder and lake names are unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Named upper Ekalluk River and elongated water passage
correspondence.finding: Both land-resource maps label the upper river Ekalluk River. The Cambridge Bay original depicts the southeastward elongated water passage, narrowing and eastward continuation. The thesis independently describes this narrow upper lake and the following eastward river reach. This establishes a named upper component without naming the selected eastern continuation.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward channel, side arrivals and broad-lake entry
correspondence.finding: The mapped eastward river and side-stream arrivals lead into the northwestern arm of the broad middle lake. The two sources agree on this river-to-lake connection at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad middle lake and selected eastern passage
correspondence.finding: The selection crosses the northern and northeastern waters of the broad lake labelled Ekalluk Lake, with the qualifier locally known as, on the 1983 map. The thesis describes the corresponding broad lake as unnamed. Its lake arms and adjacent waters are distinguishable, but a through-going eastern exit matching the selection is not established. The historical local map name is retained as a bounded lake component.

correspondence.component_scope: Transfer from Ekalluk Lake to the parallel eastern lake-and-stream corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection heads east and southeast from the broad Ekalluk Lake area into a separate parallel lake-and-stream corridor. The original map does not establish that through-link. Instead, it depicts the broad lake outlet to the south; the thesis explicitly traces that continuation southeast toward Wishbone Lake and then southwest into Ferguson Lake, whose outlet is to Wellington Bay. This is a material connection question between identifiable water corridors, not a demand for exact model-to-bank agreement.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower inland lake chain and eastward sheet crossing
correspondence.finding: The Cambridge Bay map shows the distinct elongated lake and intervening stream setting east of the Ekalluk Lake outlet. Parts of the chosen southeastern/eastward route can be located in that setting, but the entire selected sequence of lake entries, exits and its continuation over the eastern neatline is not established by the inspected material. The Ekalluk name is not extended over this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern continuation and coastal-system join
correspondence.finding: The thesis maps show a separate drainage entering western Albert Edward Bay, near the Jayco system, and distinguish Char and Fish Trap lakes within it. They do not establish the complete selected eastward transfer from the upper Ekalluk component through every lower lake/channel join. Char Lake, Fish Trap Lake and Jayco Lake therefore remain nearby disambiguation names, not adopted selected-component names.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northward approach and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected terminal is in the western Albert Edward Bay coastal setting. The thesis depicts the separate adjacent drainage mouth and Jayco mouth; ARC403 describes Albert Edward Bay as a Victoria Strait embayment. Receiving-bay identity is supported at ordinary regional scale, but the exact selected lower channel and its upstream continuity into that coast are not established. No complete terminal-through-link finding is claimed.
